metadata.jurisdiction: Global, with emphasis on low- and intermediate-resource settings
metadata.summary: The package identifies evidence-based eye care interventions spanning health promotion and prevention, screening, diagnosis and monitoring, treatment, and vision rehabilitation. It specifies relevant life stages, levels of care and material resources to support the selection and integration of interventions into health services. It is intended primarily for health-service planning in low- and middle-income settings, and its intervention lists are not exhaustive.

conditions_covered: Disorders of the eyelid and lacrimal system
target_population: People of all ages with eye conditions or vision impairment
Newborns, including preterm and/or low-birth-weight infants
People with irreversible vision impairment or blindness

prophylaxis.recommendation: Encourage more time outdoors and less intensive near-vision activity to delay myopia onset and progression.

Provide education about a healthy diet rich in vitamin A, measles and rubella immunization, and vitamin A supplementation. The PECI does not provide supplementation guidance for reducing corneal ulceration risk.

prophylaxis.type: Prophylactic management to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum
prophylaxis.recommendation: Use ophthalmic antibiotic ointment and clean the eyelids at birth.
Manage and control hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia to prevent or delay diabetic retinopathy onset and progression.
Promote trauma-prevention measures, including protective equipment during high-risk activities, alongside relevant public and occupational safety measures.
prophylaxis.target_population: People undertaking high-risk activities, including certain sports, agricultural activities, construction and welding

prophylaxis.type: Prevention of ocular allergies, inflammation and infection transmission
prophylaxis.recommendation: Counsel people to avoid irritants that may provoke ocular allergies or inflammation, and to use facial cleanliness, handwashing and separate towels to limit the spread of eye infections.

Apply the “SAFE” strategy, including antibiotic mass drug administration to lower infection prevalence, facial cleanliness and environmental improvement to reduce transmission, and eyelid surgery to reduce ongoing visual impairment. Counselling should also address appropriate disposal of human faeces to limit breeding sites for flies that spread trachoma.

infection_management.prevention: The “SAFE” strategy uses antibiotic mass drug administration to reduce prevalence, and facial cleanliness and environmental improvement to reduce transmission. Education in endemic populations also covers disposal of human faeces to limit fly breeding sites.
infection_management.management: Eyelid surgery within the “SAFE” strategy reduces the risk of continuing visual impairment.

infection_management.prevention: Apply ophthalmic antibiotic ointment and clean the eyelids at birth.

infection_management.management: Screen newborns for eye infections and refer promptly when screening identifies a condition requiring care.

infection_management.prevention: Counsel on facial cleanliness, handwashing and use of separate towels to limit spread of eye infections.

Medical treatment for infectious uveitis is included among the priority interventions; the document does not specify a regimen.

infection_management.prevention: Immunization against measles and rubella is included to reduce secondary eye conditions, including corneal opacities.

therapies_index.name: Advice to optimize the living environment for persons with vision impairment

conditions.name: Cataract
conditions.description: Clouding of the eye’s lens is treated by removing the lens and implanting an artificial intraocular lens.
conditions.epidemiology: An estimated 100 million people have moderate-to-severe distance vision impairment or blindness that could be corrected through cataract surgery. Cataract development is part of ageing.

long_term_effects: Posterior capsular opacification may occur after cataract surgery.

conditions.name: Diabetic retinopathy
conditions.description: A diabetes-related eye condition that can be prevented or delayed by controlling hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia. Early disease may be asymptomatic.
conditions.epidemiology: It is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes and a leading global cause of preventable vision impairment and blindness. If current trends persist, the estimated number of affected people rises 1.2-fold, from 146 million in 2014 to 180.6 million in 2030.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Early stages can have no symptoms; vision-threatening disease can result in vision impairment or blindness.
