conditions.description: An opacity occurring after cataract surgery for which Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy is listed when indicated.

conditions.name: corneal opacities
conditions.description: Corneal opacification is a cause of blindness for which transplantation may be indicated; some leading indications for transplantation, including eye injury and corneal infection, are avoidable.
conditions.epidemiology: Corneal opacities remain a leading cause of blindness in low- and middle-income countries.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Vision impairment or blindness may occur.

special_populations.considerations: Congenital and acquired eye conditions may interfere with visual development if detection and care are delayed. The document calls for an external eye examination and red reflex test at birth or at the first well-baby visit, with prompt or urgent referral after a positive screen.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: For congenital cataract, surgery is preferably performed within the first 3 months of life; the stated timing is 4–6 weeks for unilateral cataract and up to 8 weeks for bilateral cataract.

special_populations.considerations: This group needs measures to prevent retinopathy of prematurity, including monitoring oxygen levels and saturation, and systematic retinal screening using local, evidence-based criteria. The screening entry specifies preferably 4–5 weeks postnatal, followed by timely referral when indicated and long-term follow-up.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: The listed transpupillary diode laser treatment for retinopathy of prematurity is performed after 36 weeks postmenstrual age.

special_populations.considerations: Refractive error, particularly myopia, is expected to become more common in this age group. Vision screening before school and within school health services can identify reduced visual acuity and other eye conditions; timely correction or referral is important. Education also addresses time spent outdoors, intensive near-vision activity and adherence to spectacle use.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: For children with amblyopia who do not improve with spectacles alone, the document lists patching of the non-amblyopic eye or pharmacological cycloplegic penalization. Pediatric cataract surgery is addressed separately from adult surgery because its personnel and equipment requirements differ.

special_populations.considerations: Near- and distance-vision impairment are more prevalent at older ages. The document emphasizes accessible, active assessment of visual acuity rather than standalone screening of the general adult population. It cites WHO guidance recommending primary-care visual acuity assessment for people aged ≥60 years, followed by timely comprehensive eye care.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: For indicated near-vision correction, the document lists readymade reading spectacles for adults aged ≥40 years; clinically significant anisometropia and astigmatism require custom-made reading spectacles.

special_populations.considerations: Diabetic retinopathy may be asymptomatic early in its course. The document supports systematic retinal screening to detect vision-threatening disease, annually or biennially depending on the setting, with referral and timely treatment when indicated. Control of hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia can prevent or delay its onset and progression.

special_populations.population: People with irreversible vision impairment or blindness
special_populations.considerations: Vision rehabilitation is tailored to the person's functional needs and priorities. The listed approaches include assistive products, changes to living and working environments, orientation and mobility training, and access to psychological support.

special_populations.population: People at risk of acute angle-closure glaucoma
special_populations.considerations: The document calls for counselling about symptoms of developing acute angle-closure glaucoma and instructing those at risk to seek immediate ophthalmic attention if symptoms occur.

special_populations.population: Underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries
special_populations.considerations: The burden of eye conditions and vision impairment is greater in underserved groups, including rural residents, people with low incomes, women, older people, people with certain disabilities, indigenous populations and ethnic minorities. Costs, limited availability of services and their concentration in urban secondary or tertiary hospitals impede access; the document emphasizes stronger primary eye care and effective referral pathways.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with near or distance refractive error
decision_rules: Provide spectacles to correct near or distance refractive error.
Make refractive and optical services available at primary care facilities or as close to them as feasible.

recommended_regimens.name: Spectacle correction of refractive error in adults
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide corrective spectacles for adults with near or distance refractive error.

alternative_regimens.name: contact lenses
alternative_regimens.summary: Contact lenses can correct reduced vision caused by refractive error.

alternative_regimens.name: laser surgery
alternative_regimens.summary: Laser surgery is another means of correcting refractive error.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Adult spectacle provision is listed for primary plus, secondary and tertiary care. The document prioritizes timely access to prescription spectacles near people's homes.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Children with refractive error
decision_rules: Provide spectacles for refractive error detected in children.
Coordinate school-based screening and spectacle provision with eye care professionals at other care levels when examination, refraction or dispensing is needed.

recommended_regimens.name: Spectacle correction for refractive error in children
recommended_regimens.summary: Correct childhood refractive error with spectacles, including through school health programmes where applicable.

supportive_care: Counsel children, parents, caregivers and teachers about adherence to spectacle wear.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: School-based provision may require referral or coordination for refraction and optical dispensing.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People aged >40 years requiring near-vision correction
decision_rules: Measure and record near visual acuity with a standard near-reading chart before providing readymade reading spectacles when indicated.
Use individually made reading spectacles for individuals with clinically significant anisometropia and astigmatism.

recommended_regimens.name: Readymade reading spectacles for the correction of presbyopia
recommended_regimens.summary: Supply readymade reading spectacles when near-vision testing indicates a need for them.

alternative_regimens.name: Custom made reading spectacles
alternative_regimens.summary: Provide individually made reading spectacles rather than readymade spectacles.

response_assessment.method: Measure and document near visual acuity with a standard near-reading chart.
response_assessment.interpretation: Use the result to determine whether reading spectacles are indicated.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The treatment table describes eligibility as aged >40 years and also labels the life-course group aged ≥40 years; the primary-care package states 40 years and over. Readymade spectacles can be supplied in community and primary care settings.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Children with amblyopia
decision_rules: Use spectacles before considering patching or pharmacological penalization; the latter options are described for children whose amblyopia does not improve with spectacles alone.

recommended_regimens.name: spectacles
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide spectacle correction before moving to treatments specified for amblyopia that persists despite spectacles.

response_assessment.method: Assess whether amblyopia improves with spectacles alone.
response_assessment.interpretation: If improvement is insufficient, patching or pharmacological penalization can be considered.

supportive_care: Counsel children and caregivers on adherence to the treatment regimen.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Children with amblyopia who do not improve with spectacles alone; patching is listed from 28 days to 15 years
decision_rules: If spectacles alone do not improve amblyopia, patch the nonamblyopic eye as a treatment option.

recommended_regimens.name: Patching for the treatment of amblyopia
recommended_regimens.summary: Patch the nonamblyopic eye in a child whose amblyopia has not improved sufficiently with spectacles.

alternative_regimens.name: Pharmacological (cycloplegic penalization) treatment for amblyopia
alternative_regimens.summary: Produce cycloplegia in the nonamblyopic eye as another treatment for amblyopia persisting despite spectacles.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Children who do not improve with spectacles alone; the treatment table specifies aged 3–15 years.

supportive_care: Counsel the child and caregivers about treatment adherence.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Both patching and pharmacological penalization are listed at secondary and tertiary care levels; the document does not rank one above the other.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with strabismus for whom an operation is indicated, from early childhood to later adulthood
decision_rules: Consider an extraocular muscle operation when surgical treatment of strabismus is indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Strabismus surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat indicated strabismus by operating on the extraocular muscles.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The table places this operation at tertiary care level.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with cataract for whom surgery is indicated
decision_rules: Remove the clouded lens and implant an intraocular lens when adult cataract surgery is indicated.
Select among the listed surgical techniques in light of resources and costs; the package designates SICS as essential without excluding the other included techniques.

recommended_regimens.name: Small incision cataract surgery (SICS) with IOL Implantation
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat adult cataract with small-incision surgery and IOL implantation when indicated; this technique is marked essential in the intervention table.

alternative_regimens.name: Large-incision, extra capsular cataract surgery with IOL (ECCE-IOL)
alternative_regimens.summary: Remove the cataract using extracapsular extraction and implant an intraocular lens. The document describes ECCE as safe and effective, but states that recovery and postoperative uncorrected vision are inferior to those with phacoemulsification and SICS.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Included as a surgical option; the techniques differ substantially in resource requirements and costs.

alternative_regimens.name: Suture less, small incision phacoemulsification with IOL implantation
alternative_regimens.summary: Remove the cataract by phacoemulsification and implant an intraocular lens. The document describes phacoemulsification and SICS as comparable in safety and efficacy.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Included as a surgical option; instruments and consumables for phacoemulsification can limit its use in lower-resource settings.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: All three adult cataract procedures are listed at secondary and tertiary levels. The document reports that postoperative visual results can be suboptimal in some settings and emphasizes quality of service delivery.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Children with congenital, infantile or pediatric cataract
decision_rules: Operate early to prevent deprivation amblyopia and delayed visual development.
For congenital cataract, the stated preferred window is within first 3 months of life; the document separately specifies 4–6 weeks for unilateral cataract and up to 8 weeks for bilateral cataract.

recommended_regimens.name: Pediatric cataract surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Undertake early pediatric cataract surgery to prevent deprivation amblyopia.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: For congenital cataract, preferably within first 3 months of life; for unilateral cataract, 4–6 weeks; for bilateral cataract, up to 8 weeks.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The table locates pediatric cataract surgery at tertiary care level and notes that its personnel and equipment needs differ from those of adult cataract surgery.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with posterior capsular opacity after cataract surgery, when intervention is indicated
decision_rules: Manage indicated posterior capsular opacity following cataract surgery with Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy.

recommended_regimens.name: Management of posterior capsular opacification
recommended_regimens.summary: Use Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy for posterior capsular opacity arising after cataract surgery.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People of any age with glaucoma requiring medical management
decision_rules: Use a tolerated and effective medication, alone or combined with other medication, that lowers intraocular pressure sufficiently to attain and maintain the target pressure.

recommended_regimens.name: Medical therapy for persons with glaucoma
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat glaucoma medically with single or combined therapy selected according to tolerability, efficacy and the target intraocular pressure.

response_assessment.method: Monitor intraocular pressure against the target pressure.
response_assessment.interpretation: Treatment should reach and maintain the target pressure to reduce the risk of further progression.

supportive_care: Counsel patients and caregivers about adherence to long-term treatment.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The medicine list groups Pilocarpine eye drops, Latanaprost, Timolol maleate, Oral acetazolamide and Intravenous mannitol under miotics and glaucoma preparations. The document does not specify a preferred drug sequence. Medical therapy is listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with acute or chronic angle closure glaucoma, or in whom prevention of angle closure glaucoma is indicated
decision_rules: Use laser peripheral iridotomy when indicated to prevent or manage acute or chronic angle closure glaucoma.

recommended_regimens.name: Laser peripheral iridotomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform peripheral iridotomy with Nd:YAG Laser or Argon Green Laser when indicated for prevention or management of angle closure glaucoma.

supportive_care: Inform people at risk of acute angle-closure glaucoma about symptoms and the need for immediate ophthalmic attention if they occur.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The table lists this procedure for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with glaucoma for whom selective laser trabeculoplasty is indicated
decision_rules: Consider selective laser trabeculoplasty when indicated for a person with glaucoma.

recommended_regimens.name: Selective laser trabeculoplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat indicated glaucoma with selective laser trabeculoplasty.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The intervention table lists secondary and tertiary care; provision at secondary level depends on national availability, cost–effectiveness and available personnel.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with glaucoma for whom filtration surgery and/or iridectomy is indicated
decision_rules: Perform glaucoma filtration surgery and/or iridectomy when indicated, with or without antifibrotic agents.

recommended_regimens.name: Filtration surgery (i.e. trabeculectomy) and iridectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Use filtration surgery and/or iridectomy for indicated glaucoma, optionally with antifibrotic agents.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care; the secondary-care option depends on national availability, cost–effectiveness and personnel.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with glaucoma for whom diode laser cyclophotocoagulation is indicated
decision_rules: Use diode laser cyclophotocoagulation when indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Cyclophotocoagulation
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform diode laser cyclophotocoagulation for indicated glaucoma.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed at tertiary care level; the document does not specify its order relative to other glaucoma procedures.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People of any age with uncontrolled glaucoma for whom drainage devices are indicated
decision_rules: Consider a glaucoma drainage device when glaucoma is uncontrolled and its use is indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Glaucoma surgery – glaucoma drainage devices
recommended_regimens.summary: Implant a glaucoma drainage device for indicated uncontrolled glaucoma.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed at tertiary care level; the document does not define a required sequence of prior treatments.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Children with congenital or pediatric glaucoma
decision_rules: Treat congenital or pediatric glaucoma with goniotomy or trabeculotomy.

recommended_regimens.name: Angle surgery (i.e. goniotomy or trabeculotomy) for children with congenital glaucoma
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform goniotomy or trabeculotomy for childhood glaucoma.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed at tertiary care level.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People of any age with chemical exposure to the eye
decision_rules: Irrigate the exposed eye urgently and refer when indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Irrigation of the eye in cases of chemical exposure and referral, where indicated
recommended_regimens.summary: Immediately irrigate after ocular chemical exposure using Ringer lactate solution, normal saline or clean water.

supportive_care: Arrange urgent referral to an appropriate care level for eye injuries.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Irrigation is listed for community, primary, secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People of any age with blunt injury, corneal abrasion, foreign body, sharp or penetrating injury, or burns
decision_rules: Provide immediate first aid for eye injury and arrange urgent referral to the appropriate level of care.

recommended_regimens.name: Provision of immediate first aid care and referral for eye injury
recommended_regimens.summary: Give immediate first aid for the listed forms of ocular injury, followed by urgent referral.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: This pathway is included in the primary eye care package; injuries exceeding primary-care capabilities require referral.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People of any age with corneal abrasions, erosions or small perforations for which treatment is indicated
decision_rules: Manage corneal abrasion, erosion or small perforation when indicated; provide primary-level care only within its defined scope and refer cases requiring more advanced treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: Management of corneal abrasions, erosions, and/or small perforations, where indicated.
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide surgical or nonsurgical management of indicated corneal abrasion, erosion or small perforation.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The intervention has a narrower scope at primary care than at secondary or tertiary care. The equipment list includes a bandage contact lens and Cyanoacrylate glue for this intervention.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People of any age with infective or allergic conjunctivitis, dry eye disease, blepharitis, ocular foreign body or keratitis
decision_rules: Provide medical management for the relevant adnexal or ocular-surface disorder, with the scope of primary-care treatment differing from that available at higher levels.

recommended_regimens.name: Medical therapy for adnexa and ocular surface related disorders
recommended_regimens.summary: Medically treat the specified adnexal or ocular-surface condition; treatment for some of these disorders is principally directed at symptom relief.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for primary, secondary and tertiary care. The document does not provide condition-specific drug selection or dosing in this treatment pathway.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People of any age presenting in primary care with red eye or abnormal lashes
decision_rules: Offer treatment or first aid for red eye or abnormal lashes, advise follow-up, and refer promptly if improvement is limited or absent.
For loss of vision, ocular swelling or a growth on the eyeball, counsel the person and refer immediately.

recommended_regimens.name: Provision of first aid care and referral for ocular discomfort (red eye, vision loss, and/or external eye conditions)
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide initial primary-care treatment or first aid for ocular discomfort and use the described referral thresholds.

response_assessment.method: Assess improvement in red eye or abnormal lashes.
response_assessment.interpretation: Little or no improvement calls for timely referral.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Immediate referral is specified for loss of vision, ocular swelling or a growth on the eyeball.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with keratoconus whose best corrected vision does not improve with spectacles alone
decision_rules: Use contact lenses to improve best corrected vision if spectacles alone do not provide adequate improvement.

recommended_regimens.name: Contact lenses for keratoconus
recommended_regimens.summary: Fit contact lenses for keratoconus when spectacle correction alone does not improve best corrected vision.

response_assessment.interpretation: Lack of improvement with spectacles identifies the population for contact lenses.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with demonstrated progressive keratoconus or corneal ectasia
decision_rules: Consider corneal cross-linking when progression of keratoconus or corneal ectasia has been demonstrated.

recommended_regimens.name: Corneal cross-linking for the treatment of keratoconus
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform corneal cross-linking for demonstrated progressive keratoconus or corneal ectasia.

response_assessment.method: Establish whether keratoconus or corneal ectasia is progressive.
response_assessment.interpretation: Demonstrated progression is the stated eligibility criterion.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed at tertiary care level; the intervention is included in the package but is not marked essential.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with severe, symptomatic dry eye for whom punctal occlusion is indicated
decision_rules: Consider punctal occlusion for symptomatic relief when severe dry eye warrants this procedure.

recommended_regimens.name: Punctal occlusion for dry eye
recommended_regimens.summary: Occlude the punctum to alleviate symptoms of severe dry eye when indicated.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care; the document does not specify a prerequisite treatment sequence.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with hordeolum or chalazion for whom a procedure is indicated
decision_rules: Perform incision and drainage or curettage when indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Incision and drainage of hordeolum and chalazion
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat an indicated hordeolum or chalazion by incision and drainage or curettage.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed at secondary and tertiary care levels.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Children aged 6–12 months with congenital nasolacrimal obstruction for whom probing is indicated
decision_rules: Treat indicated congenital nasolacrimal obstruction by probing.

recommended_regimens.name: Probing for congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction
recommended_regimens.summary: Probe the nasolacrimal duct to treat indicated congenital obstruction.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with pterygium for whom surgery is indicated, including advanced disease affecting vision
decision_rules: Perform surgical excision with a conjunctival autograft when indicated; surgery is often required in advanced cases affecting vision.

recommended_regimens.name: Pterygium surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Excise the pterygium and place a conjunctival autograft, with or without mitomycin C.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People for whom a corneal transplant is indicated
decision_rules: Consider corneal transplantation when indicated; the document does not restrict this intervention to a single corneal diagnosis.

recommended_regimens.name: Corneal transplantation surgery – keratoplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform penetrating, partial-thickness or lamellar keratoplasty when a corneal transplant is indicated.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The transplant is listed at tertiary care level. Limited graft-tissue availability and out-of-pocket costs can obstruct access; the document also emphasizes prevention of avoidable indications such as ocular trauma and corneal infection.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People for whom amniotic membrane transplantation is indicated
decision_rules: Use an amniotic membrane graft when indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Amniotic membrane graft
recommended_regimens.summary: Transplant an amniotic membrane graft when clinically indicated.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed at tertiary care level; the treatment table does not identify a narrower diagnostic indication.

treatment_pathways.condition: Disorders of the eyelid and lacrimal system
treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with an eyelid disorder for which surgery is indicated
decision_rules: Select eyelid surgery when indicated for pediatric ptosis, blepharoptosis, entropion, ectropion, trichiasis or another listed eyelid condition.

recommended_regimens.name: Eyelid surgery – general
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide indicated eyelid surgery, including tarsorrhaphy, correction of pediatric ptosis, blepharoptosis, entropion or ectropion, blepharoplasty, trichiasis treatment or eyelid reconstruction.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with infectious or non-infectious uveitis, from later childhood to later adulthood
decision_rules: Provide medical management appropriate to infectious or non-infectious uveitis.

recommended_regimens.name: Medical management for uveitis
recommended_regimens.summary: Medically treat infectious or non-infectious uveitis.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care. The treatment table does not specify disease-specific medicines, treatment order or dosage.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with neovascular age-related macular degeneration for whom treatment is indicated
decision_rules: Use intraocular anti-VEGF treatment for the neovascular form of age-related macular degeneration; the document limits this stated effective treatment indication to the neovascular form.

recommended_regimens.name: Antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Administer intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment for indicated neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care. The document describes intravitreal anti-VEGF as the gold standard for a range of retinal disorders but notes that cost restricts its availability in many LMICs.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with myopic macular degeneration for whom treatment is indicated
decision_rules: Use intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy when treatment of myopic macular degeneration is indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat indicated myopic macular degeneration with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care; cost limits availability in many LMICs.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with diabetes, particularly those with vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy or indicated diabetic eye disease
decision_rules: Combine management of hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia with systematic retinal screening and timely treatment when disease requiring intervention is identified.
Use intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy or retinal laser photocoagulation for indicated diabetic eye disease; the document does not rank these options for a particular disease stage.

recommended_regimens.name: Antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy for diabetic eye disease when indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Retinal laser photocoagulation
recommended_regimens.summary: Use indicated retinal laser treatment, which may comprise pan retinal, focal or grid photocoagulation.

response_assessment.timepoint: Annually or biennially, depending on the setting
response_assessment.method: Systematic retinal screening by trained eye-care personnel using ophthalmoscopy or retinal imaging with local interpretation or centralized grading.
response_assessment.interpretation: Detect vision-threatening disease early and refer for timely treatment when indicated.

supportive_care: Educate and counsel people with diabetes about controlling hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia, and refer when appropriate.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Both intravitreal anti-VEGF and retinal laser photocoagulation are listed for secondary and tertiary care. The package does not provide protocols for medical management of diabetic retinopathy risk factors.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Infants with retinopathy of prematurity for whom treatment is indicated
decision_rules: Identify disease through systematic screening of infants born preterm and/or with low birth weight, refer promptly when indicated, and provide transpupillary diode laser treatment for treatable disease.

recommended_regimens.name: Transpupillary diode laser for the treatment of retinopathy of prematurity
recommended_regimens.summary: Apply transpupillary diode laser therapy to reduce the risk of visual impairment or blindness from retinopathy of prematurity.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Treatment performed after 36 weeks postmenstrual age.

response_assessment.timepoint: A few weeks after birth; preferably at 4–5 weeks postnatal
response_assessment.method: Systematic retinal screening using local, evidence-based eligibility criteria.
response_assessment.interpretation: Refer promptly for treatment when indicated.

supportive_care: Monitor oxygen levels and saturation in preterm infants as a preventive measure.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Laser treatment is listed at tertiary care level. The document does not designate anti-VEGF treatment as a selected retinopathy-of-prematurity intervention in its treatment table.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with a vitreoretinal disorder for which laser treatment is indicated
decision_rules: Select pan retinal, focal or grid retinal photocoagulation according to the indicated vitreoretinal disorder; the document does not give condition-specific selection criteria.

recommended_regimens.name: Retinal laser photocoagulation
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide indicated laser photocoagulation for a vitreoretinal disorder.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with indicated retinal detachment, macular hole, advanced proliferative diabetic retinopathy, complications of cataract surgery, or penetrating or blunt ocular trauma
decision_rules: Use vitreoretinal surgery, including vitrectomy when appropriate, for the listed conditions if surgery is indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Vitreoretinal surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform vitrectomy or another indicated vitreoretinal operation, with or without adjunctive dyes and/or triamcinolone.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed at tertiary care level.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Children with retinoblastoma, from the neonatal period to age <5 years
decision_rules: Manage retinoblastoma using surgery and/or chemotherapy, laser treatment or cryotherapy; the document does not define how to choose among these modalities.

recommended_regimens.name: Management for retinoblastoma
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat childhood retinoblastoma with indicated surgical and/or nonsurgical modalities, including chemotherapy, laser and cryotherapy.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Care requires a multidisciplinary approach and is listed at tertiary care level. The medicine list identifies Vincristine IV infusion, Carboplatin IV infusion and Etoposide IV infusion as chemotherapy agents for retinoblastoma, with doses adjusted based on age; it does not prescribe a combination or sequence.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with an intraocular malignancy for which evisceration or enucleation is indicated
decision_rules: Perform evisceration or enucleation when indicated for intraocular malignancy.

recommended_regimens.name: Evisceration and Enucleation
recommended_regimens.summary: Use the indicated globe-removal procedure for intraocular malignancy.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care. The document does not state a required prior cancer-treatment sequence.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with a blind painful eye not amenable to alternative treatment
decision_rules: Consider evisceration or enucleation when a blind painful eye cannot be managed by an alternative treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: Evisceration and Enucleation
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform the indicated procedure for a blind painful eye that cannot be treated otherwise.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with infection or inflammation after ocular surgery for whom management is indicated
decision_rules: Manage postoperative ocular infection or inflammation when indicated.

recommended_regimens.name: Management of postoperative infections/ Inflammation
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide surgical or nonsurgical management of indicated infection or inflammation following eye surgery.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Listed for secondary and tertiary care; no organism-specific treatment algorithm is provided.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Populations in which trachoma is endemic
decision_rules: Use the combined SAFE strategy to address visual consequences, prevalence and transmission of trachoma.

recommended_regimens.name: SAFE
recommended_regimens.summary: Combine eyelid surgery [S] to lower the risk of ongoing visual impairment, antibiotic [A] mass drug administration to reduce prevalence, and facial cleanliness [F] plus environmental improvement [E] to reduce transmission.

supportive_care: Include counselling about appropriate disposal of human faeces to reduce breeding sites for flies that transmit trachoma.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The strategy is described for endemic populations; the document does not give an antibiotic name or dosing regimen for SAFE.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: People with vision impairment or blindness who need vision rehabilitation
decision_rules: Tailor rehabilitation to the person's affected visual functions, needs and priorities.
Arrange psychological support, assistive products, environmental adaptations or skills training according to individual need rather than applying every intervention to every person.

recommended_regimens.name: Referral to vision rehabilitation specialists, group programmes and psychological supports for persons with vision impairment or blindness
recommended_regimens.summary: Refer for or provide individual or group mental-health support addressing depression, anxiety, fatigue or grief associated with vision loss.

recommended_regimens.name: Provision of optical assistive products, including filters
recommended_regimens.summary: Prescribe optical devices such as magnifiers or telescopes and train the person in their use when applicable.

recommended_regimens.name: Provision of non-optical assistive products
recommended_regimens.summary: Prescribe and provide training in suitable non-optical aids for everyday activities.

recommended_regimens.name: Provision of electronic assistive products
recommended_regimens.summary: Advise on, recommend and teach the use of suitable electronic assistive products.

recommended_regimens.name: Orientation and mobility training
recommended_regimens.summary: Teach spatial orientation and safer independent movement, potentially including sighted-guide or basic protection techniques.

alternative_regimens.name: Advice to optimize the living environment for persons with vision impairment
alternative_regimens.summary: Advise on adapting living, educational or work environments, improving lighting, managing daily activities and reducing fall risks.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Tailor to the person's surroundings and needs; this intervention is included but not marked essential in the rehabilitation table.

alternative_regimens.name: Vision skills training
alternative_regimens.summary: Teach appropriate visual skills, such as scanning for visual-field loss or reading strategies for central-field loss.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Use according to the person's functional deficit; this intervention is included but not marked essential in the rehabilitation table.

response_assessment.method: Assess functional vision and individual priorities.
response_assessment.interpretation: Match interventions to the visual functions and everyday activities affected.

supportive_care: Coordinate referral to trained eye care and rehabilitation professionals when examination, diagnosis, prescription or training exceeds community or primary-care capabilities.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Community-based provision or replacement of some assistive products can occur through school health or community rehabilitation programmes, with coordination at higher levels of care.

recommendations.statement: Deliver eye health promotion and education throughout the health system, placing particular emphasis on simple education and counselling in community and primary care.
recommendations.context: All levels of care.
recommendations.rationale: Greater awareness can support prevention, timely assessment and use of eye care services.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Explain to parents, caregivers and teachers that intensive near-vision activity is a risk factor for myopia and that more time outdoors is protective.
recommendations.context: Infants, children and adolescents; educational priority in Table 1.
recommendations.rationale: These behaviours are relevant to the onset and progression of myopia and the prevention of high myopia.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Educate children and their parents, caregivers and teachers about adherence to spectacle wear.
recommendations.context: Educational priority in Table 1.
recommendations.rationale: Uncorrected refractive error can adversely affect education and other aspects of life.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide education on a healthy diet rich in vitamin A, measles and rubella immunization, and vitamin A supplementation; include the listed immunizations and supplementation as clinical preventive measures.
recommendations.context: Children; educational and clinical priority in Table 1. The PECI does not provide supplementation guidance for reducing corneal ulceration risk.
recommendations.rationale: These measures help prevent secondary eye conditions.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Monitor oxygen levels and saturation in preterm infants.
recommendations.context: Clinical preventive priority in Table 1.
recommendations.rationale: The measure is intended to prevent retinopathy of prematurity.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use ophthalmic antibiotic ointment and clean the eyelids at birth.
recommendations.context: Clinical preventive priority for neonates in Table 1.
recommendations.rationale: These measures are intended to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Educate and counsel people with diabetes about controlling hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia, arrange referral when indicated, and provide clinical management of those risk factors.
recommendations.context: Educational and clinical priority in Table 1; medical management of these risk factors is outside the PECI intervention package.
recommendations.rationale: Controlling these factors can prevent or delay diabetic retinopathy onset and progression.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Counsel adults about smoking, ultraviolet exposure, prolonged digital-device use and long-term corticosteroid use as applicable to the eye conditions linked to each exposure.
recommendations.context: Educational priority in Table 1: smoking is linked to age-related macular degeneration, dry eye and cataract; ultraviolet exposure to cataract and pterygium; prolonged digital-device use to dry eye disease; and long-term corticosteroid use to cataract and glaucoma.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Inform people at risk of acute angle-closure glaucoma about its developing symptoms and instruct them to seek immediate ophthalmic care if symptoms arise.
recommendations.context: Educational priority in Table 1.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Raise awareness of the importance of regular comprehensive eye examinations in groups at high risk.
recommendations.context: Table 1 identifies older adults, people with diabetes, people with certain genetic conditions such as sickle cell disease, and those with a family history of glaucoma or age-related macular degeneration.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Counsel people with chronic eye conditions and their caregivers about adhering to prescribed treatment.
recommendations.context: Educational priority in Table 1; examples include glaucoma and amblyopia.
recommendations.rationale: Counselling is intended to improve long-term treatment adherence.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Increase public awareness of common vision problems and available interventions, including spectacles and cataract surgery.
recommendations.context: Educational priority in Table 1, intended to increase demand for eye care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Promote prevention of ocular injury, including provision and use of protective equipment during high-risk activities and work.
recommendations.context: Table 1 cites certain sports, agriculture, construction and welding, and examples of protection include masks, goggles and visors.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Counsel people on eye health practices, avoidance of irritants, and prevention of ocular infection spread through facial cleanliness, handwashing and separate towels.
recommendations.context: Educational priority for all ages in Table 1; in trachoma-endemic populations, also address appropriate disposal of human faeces.
recommendations.rationale: Avoiding irritants can help prevent ocular allergy and inflammation; faeces disposal limits breeding sites for flies that transmit trachoma.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority areas of health promotion and prevention in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Screen newborns for neonatal infections and congenital or acquired eye conditions, and refer promptly when screening is positive.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 2: neonatal period, <1month, preferably within 72 hrs of birth, or at first contact with a well-baby clinic. The described assessment includes an external eye examination and red reflex test.
recommendations.rationale: Timely detection and intervention can prevent adverse effects of delayed visual development.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority screening interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Screen pre-school children for reduced visual acuity, infection or inflammation, amblyopia and strabismus, with timely referral when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 2 for children aged 3–5 years.
recommendations.rationale: Early detection and access to appropriate care can reduce the impact of untreated visual impairment.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority screening interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide vision screening and an eye examination to school-age children to identify reduced visual acuity, infection or inflammation, amblyopia and strabismus, followed by timely referral when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 2 for ages 5–18 years; community delivery is specified in the context of school health initiatives.
recommendations.rationale: Timely correction and other eye care can mitigate the effects of unaddressed vision impairment.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority screening interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Actively assess near and distance vision in older people and arrange suitable interventions or referral when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 2 for adults aged ≥60 years; accessible assessment may be provided in community or primary care. Standalone visual screening programmes for adult populations are not currently supported by evidence.
recommendations.rationale: Near- and distance-vision impairment is more prevalent in older age groups.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority screening interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Systematically screen preterm and/or low-birth-weight infants for retinopathy of prematurity and refer promptly when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 2; screening starts a few weeks after birth according to local evidence-based criteria, preferably at 4–5 weeks postnatal.
recommendations.rationale: Detection and timely treatment can reduce subsequent vision impairment or blindness.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority screening interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Systematically screen people with diabetes for diabetic retinopathy and refer when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 2, from later childhood through later adulthood. The screening discussion describes annual or biennial retinal assessment, depending on the setting.
recommendations.rationale: Early identification of vision-threatening disease, followed by timely treatment, can avert vision impairment.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority screening interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Make distance, near and pinhole visual acuity measurement and external eye assessment by torchlight available in community, primary, secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.context: Essential examinations at every care level in Table 3; the external assessment considers the eye and surrounding structures, including shape, colour, size, position, direction and eyelid closure.
recommendations.rationale: These assessments help identify visual impairment and visible abnormalities for appropriate referral.
recommendations.source_heading: Essential clinical examinations for diagnosis and monitoring of eye conditions

recommendations.statement: Provide subjective refraction as a primary-plus service and at secondary and tertiary levels; provide direct ophthalmoscopy and fundus photography as primary-plus services and at secondary and tertiary levels.
recommendations.context: Level-of-care designations in Table 3.
recommendations.source_heading: Essential clinical examinations for diagnosis and monitoring of eye conditions

recommendations.statement: Make preferential-looking visual acuity testing, slit lamp examination, automated refraction, retinoscopy, visual field testing, contrast sensitivity assessment, colour vision assessment, tonometry, keratometry and optical and/or ultrasound biometry available at secondary and tertiary levels.
recommendations.context: Essential examinations and level-of-care designations in Table 3; preferential-looking testing is for infants and preverbal children.
recommendations.source_heading: Essential clinical examinations for diagnosis and monitoring of eye conditions

recommendations.statement: Make indirect ophthalmoscopy, gonioscopy, ultrasonography, pachymetry, binocular vision assessment, Duochrome, optical coherence tomography (OCT), dry eye assessment and functional vision assessment available at secondary and tertiary levels.
recommendations.context: Essential examinations and level-of-care designations in Table 3. Cost limits OCT availability in many low- and middle-income countries; additional glaucoma and anterior-segment OCT features are desirable at tertiary level.
recommendations.source_heading: Essential clinical examinations for diagnosis and monitoring of eye conditions

recommendations.statement: Make corneal topography available at tertiary level.
recommendations.context: Level-of-care designation in Table 3.
recommendations.source_heading: Essential clinical examinations for diagnosis and monitoring of eye conditions

recommendations.statement: Prioritize refractive and optical services and diabetic retinopathy screening at primary care facilities or as close to them as possible.
recommendations.context: Countries with more developed health systems or additional resources should expand primary care assessment and interventions through primary-plus services.
recommendations.rationale: The document identifies substantial population need for these services.
recommendations.source_heading: Clinical examinations for diagnosis and monitoring

recommendations.statement: Provide spectacles to correct adults’ near and distance refractive error.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from later youth to later adulthood; primary-plus, secondary and tertiary care are listed.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide spectacles to children with refractive error.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early childhood through later adolescence; community provision is described in the context of school health programmes and coordination with eye care professionals.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Measure and record near visual acuity with a standard reading chart and provide readymade reading spectacles when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential community and primary-care intervention in Table 4 for adults aged ≥40 years. The intervention description also says >40 years. Clinically significant anisometropia and astigmatism require custom-made reading spectacles.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Consider patching the nonamblyopic eye in children whose amblyopia has not improved with spectacles alone.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4 for ages 28 days to 15 years; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use pharmacological cycloplegic penalization of the nonamblyopic eye as a treatment option when a child’s amblyopia does not improve with spectacles alone.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4 for ages 3–15 years; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Perform extraocular muscle surgery for strabismus when indicated.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4, from early childhood through later adulthood; tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Offer Small incision cataract surgery (SICS) with IOL Implantation to adults with cataract when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use Large-incision, extra capsular cataract surgery with IOL (ECCE-IOL) for adults with cataract when indicated.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4; secondary and tertiary care. Its recovery time and uncorrected postoperative vision are reported as inferior to those of phacoemulsification and SICS.
recommendations.rationale: The package includes different adult cataract procedures because their resource needs and costs differ.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use Suture less, small incision phacoemulsification with IOL implantation for adults with cataract when indicated.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.rationale: The package includes different adult cataract procedures because their resource needs and costs differ.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide early surgery for congenital, infantile or pediatric cataract.
recommendations.context: Essential tertiary-care intervention in Table 4; for congenital cataract, preferably within the first 3 months of life; for unilateral cataract, 4–6 weeks; for bilateral cataract, up to 8 weeks.
recommendations.rationale: Early treatment is intended to prevent deprivation amblyopia.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Treat posterior capsular opacity following cataract surgery with Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from later childhood through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use one or a combination of tolerated and effective glaucoma medicines sufficient to attain and maintain the target intraocular pressure.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention for all ages in Table 4; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.rationale: Reducing intraocular pressure is intended to lower the risk of further progression.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use laser peripheral iridotomy with Nd:YAG Laser or Argon Green Laser for prevention or management of acute and chronic angle-closure glaucoma when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use diode laser cyclophotocoagulation for glaucoma when indicated.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4, from early through later adulthood; tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Offer selective laser trabeculoplasty for glaucoma when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early through later adulthood; secondary or tertiary care depending on country availability, cost–effectiveness and available personnel.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Perform glaucoma filtration surgery and/or iridectomy, with or without antifibrotic agents, when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early through later adulthood; secondary or tertiary care depending on country availability, cost–effectiveness and available personnel.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use goniotomy or trabeculotomy to treat congenital and pediatric glaucoma.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4 for early childhood; tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Consider glaucoma drainage devices for uncontrolled glaucoma when indicated.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4 for all ages; tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Immediately irrigate an eye exposed to chemicals with Ringer lactate solution, normal saline or clean water, and refer when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4 for all ages at community, primary, secondary and tertiary levels.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Manage corneal abrasions, erosions and/or small perforations when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential surgical or non-surgical intervention in Table 4 for all ages; the scope of primary-level care differs from that available at secondary and tertiary levels.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide medical treatment for applicable adnexal and ocular-surface conditions, including infective or allergic conjunctivitis, dry eye disease, blepharitis, ocular foreign body and keratitis.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4 for all ages; primary-level delivery has a narrower scope than secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use contact lenses to improve best-corrected vision in people with keratoconus who do not obtain sufficient improvement from spectacles alone.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early adolescence through early adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use punctal occlusion for symptomatic relief in severe dry eye when indicated.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4, from early adolescence through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Treat hordeolum or chalazion with incision and drainage or curettage when indicated.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4, from early childhood through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use probing to treat congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4 for children aged 6–12 months; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.condition: Disorders of the eyelid and lacrimal system
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Excise pterygium with a conjunctival autograft, with or without mitomycin C, when surgery is indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early adolescence through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use corneal cross-linking for demonstrated progressive keratoconus or corneal ectasia.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4, from early adolescence through early adulthood; tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide corneal transplantation, including penetrating, partial-thickness or lamellar keratoplasty, when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early adolescence through later adulthood; tertiary care. Access may be constrained by graft-tissue shortages and patient costs.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use amniotic membrane graft transplantation when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early adolescence through later adulthood; tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide indicated eyelid surgery for conditions including pediatric ptosis, blepharoptosis, entropion, ectropion and trichiasis, or for eyelid reconstruction.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 4, from early childhood through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care. The listed procedures also include tarsorrhaphy and blepharoplasty.
recommendations.condition: Disorders of the eyelid and lacrimal system
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide medical treatment for infectious or non-infectious uveitis.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from later childhood through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy when indicated for vitreoretinal disorders such as neovascular age-related macular degeneration, myopic macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care. Treatment cost limits availability in many low- and middle-income countries.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Use indicated retinal laser photocoagulation for vitreoretinal disorders, selecting among panretinal, focal and grid photocoagulation as appropriate.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Provide indicated vitreoretinal surgery, including vitrectomy and other appropriate procedures, for retinal detachment, macular hole, advanced proliferative diabetic retinopathy and relevant complications of cataract surgery or ocular trauma.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from early childhood through later adulthood; tertiary care. Dyes and/or triamcinolone may be used as adjuncts.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Treat retinopathy of prematurity in infants with transpupillary diode laser therapy when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential tertiary-care intervention in Table 4; treatment is performed after 36 weeks postmenstrual age.
recommendations.rationale: The intervention aims to reduce vision impairment or blindness.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Manage childhood retinoblastoma with indicated surgery and/or chemotherapy, laser treatment and cryotherapy.
recommendations.context: Essential tertiary-care intervention in Table 4 for children aged <5 years; care requires a multidisciplinary approach.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Manage infection or inflammation following ocular surgery when indicated.
recommendations.context: Essential surgical or non-surgical intervention in Table 4, from early childhood through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Perform evisceration or enucleation when indicated for an intraocular malignancy or a painful blind eye that cannot be managed with an alternative treatment.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 4, from the neonatal period through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, treatment interventions in the field of eye care

recommendations.statement: Refer people with vision impairment or blindness to appropriate rehabilitation specialists, group programmes or psychological support, or deliver suitable mental health support.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 5, from early childhood through later adulthood; support may be individual or group-based and led by mental health professionals or peers.
recommendations.rationale: The support addresses depression, anxiety, fatigue or grief associated with vision loss.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, vision rehabilitation interventions

recommendations.statement: Prescribe optical assistive products, including magnifiers, telescopes and applicable filters, and train people in their use where relevant.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 5, from early childhood through later adulthood. Community provision or replacement within school health or community rehabilitation programmes involves coordination and referral to trained eye care professionals.
recommendations.rationale: Assistive products can improve functioning with irreversible vision impairment.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, vision rehabilitation interventions

recommendations.statement: Prescribe appropriate non-optical assistive products and provide training in their use.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 5, from early childhood through later adulthood; examples include braille materials, reading stands, lamps, high-contrast items and talking or tactile watches.
recommendations.rationale: These products can support daily functioning.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, vision rehabilitation interventions

recommendations.statement: Advise on, recommend and teach the use of suitable electronic assistive products.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 5, from early childhood through later adulthood; examples include digital magnifiers, audiobooks, smartphones, tablets, computers, braille displays and accessibility software.
recommendations.rationale: These products can support daily functioning.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, vision rehabilitation interventions

recommendations.statement: Advise people with vision impairment on changes to living, educational and working environments, daily activities and lighting that can improve accessibility and independence and reduce falls.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 5, from early childhood through later adulthood.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, vision rehabilitation interventions

recommendations.statement: Offer orientation and mobility training, including applicable instruction in sighted-guide or basic protection techniques.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention in Table 5, from early childhood through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care.
recommendations.rationale: Training supports spatial orientation, movement and safer independent travel.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, vision rehabilitation interventions

recommendations.statement: Provide relevant visual-skills training, such as scanning for visual field loss or reading skills for central field loss.
recommendations.context: Intervention listed as non-essential in Table 5, from early childhood through later adulthood; secondary and tertiary care. The table also includes training addressing primary convergence insufficiency.
recommendations.source_heading: Priority, evidence-based, vision rehabilitation interventions

recommendations.statement: At primary-level facilities in low-resource settings, provide eye health education and counselling, newborn eye screening, and vision testing with general eye health assessment and referral when indicated.
recommendations.context: Interventions classified as essential in Annex 7; the newborn assessment is preferably within 72 hrs of birth, pre-school vision assessment concerns ages 3–5 years, and school-age assessment concerns ages 5–18 years.
recommendations.rationale: These interventions were selected as feasible, low-cost, high-impact services for primary care.
recommendations.source_heading: Annex 7. Recommended eye care interventions/resources that can be easily, safely and effectively delivered at primary-level health facilities in low-resource settings

recommendations.statement: At primary-level facilities, give treatment or first aid for red eye and/or abnormal eyelashes, advise on follow-up, and refer in a timely manner if improvement is slight or absent; immediately counsel and refer people with vision loss, eye swelling or a growth on the eyeball.
recommendations.context: Essential intervention for all ages in Annex 7.
recommendations.source_heading: Annex 7. Recommended eye care interventions/resources that can be easily, safely and effectively delivered at primary-level health facilities in low-resource settings

recommendations.statement: Provide immediate first aid and urgent referral for eye injury.
recommendations.context: Essential primary-care intervention for all ages in Annex 7; injuries listed include blunt trauma, corneal abrasions, foreign bodies, sharp or penetrating injuries and burns.
recommendations.source_heading: Annex 7. Recommended eye care interventions/resources that can be easily, safely and effectively delivered at primary-level health facilities in low-resource settings

recommendations.statement: Refer cases exceeding the scope of primary care to suitable eye care or rehabilitation professionals in accordance with the country’s referral system.
recommendations.context: Referral principle in Annex 7.
recommendations.source_heading: Annex 7. Recommended eye care interventions/resources that can be easily, safely and effectively delivered at primary-level health facilities in low-resource settings

recommendations.statement: Develop a national eye care sector strategic plan led by government, involving relevant sectors and programmes, aligned with broader health-sector planning and funding, and accompanied by a monitoring framework.
recommendations.context: WHO recommendation in the implementation strategy; the plan should be revised every four to five years or as needed.
recommendations.rationale: The plan guides medium-term activities toward integrated people-centred eye care.
recommendations.source_heading: The PECI in the context of the WHO Eye care in health systems: Guide for action

recommendations.statement: Use the Eye Care Situation Analysis Tool (ECSAT) before planning the eye care sector strategy to identify national priorities.
recommendations.context: WHO recommendation for Phase 1 of the implementation approach.
recommendations.rationale: The assessment provides a picture of the sector and identifies priority actions.
recommendations.source_heading: The PECI in the context of the WHO Eye care in health systems: Guide for action

recommendations.statement: Use the PECI to guide operational planning and implementation, including eye care budgets at each health-system level.
recommendations.context: WHO recommendation for Phase 3 of the implementation approach.
recommendations.source_heading: The PECI in the context of the WHO Eye care in health systems: Guide for action

Clinical: Medical management of the aforementioned risk factors for diabetic retinopathy.
Noncommunicable disease; Primary care; Health promotion
Lifestyle or behavioural risk factors for eye conditions

Providing information and counselling on the well-established lifestyle and behavioural risk factors implicated in the onset and/or progression of eye conditions, including smoking (age-related macular degeneration, dry eye and cataract); exposure to ultraviolet light (cataract and pterygium); prolonged use of digital devices (dry eye disease); and long-term use of corticosteroids (cataract and glaucoma).
Primary care; Occupational health; Health promotion; Other (tobacco cessation; sun protection initiatives)
Persons at risk of developing acute angle-closure glaucoma

Providing information and counselling on the symptoms of developing acute angle-closure glaucoma for populations or persons at risk, with instructions to seek immediate ophthalmic attention if symptoms occur.
Importance of regular comprehensive eye examinations

Health promotion initiatives to raise awareness of the importance of regular eye examinations among high risk population groups, such as older adults, people with diabetes, those with certain genetic conditions (e.g. sickle cell disease), and those with a family history of glaucoma or age-related macular degeneration.
Care of older people; Noncommunicable disease; Primary care; Health promotion
Adherence to treatment regimen for chronic eye conditions

Counselling of persons, and caregivers of persons, with chronic eye conditions (e.g. glaucoma and amblyopia) regarding the importance of adherence to the treatment regimen; this is an important strategy to improve long-term compliance with recommended treatments.
Increasing demand for eye care interventions

Generating demand for interventions through increasing awareness and engaging and empowering the public to be aware of common vision-related issues and the available interventions that exist to address them (e.g. spectacle-wear and cataract surgery).
Child health; Adolescent health; School health; Care of older people; Primary care; Occupational health; Health promotion

Targeted health promotion to improve awareness of trauma prevention strategies, including the provision and use of protective equipment (e.g. masks, protective goggles, visors, etc.) in high risk activities and industries (e.g. certain sports, agricultural activities, construction, welding).
Occupational health; Injury prevention; School health; Primary care; Health promotion
Counselling on good eye health practices and prevention strategies for the spread of eye infections⁵

Counselling persons on good eye health practices, avoiding irritants to prevent ocular allergies and inflammation; and measures to prevent the spread of ocular infections including facial cleanliness, hand washing and separate towel use.
Primary care; School health; Occupational health; Health promotion
